meta.rule: Only what you have proven you own and confirmed is scanned.

rule: Scanning your external surface is active scanning, so Vedette sets two conditions. First, you prove ownership of each target: a domain with a DNS TXT record (re-checked right before every scan); a public IP you type in with a token file served on it or a reverse DNS name under one of your proved domains (re-checked right before every scan; the proof lasts 30 days and the box checks it again by itself); a public IP the box finds as its own egress address is proved by that detection and renewed each time the box sees it. Second, an administrator with two-step sign-in confirms that your company owns it and that the scan is authorized: the first Scan now of a target records that confirmation, with the exact sentence shown beside the button. Until then the button stays locked for everyone else. Every verification and scan is written to the audit log.

help.how: The box asks three public "what is my IP" services over HTTPS: checkip.amazonaws.com (AWS), icanhazip.com (Cloudflare) and ifconfig.me/ip (Google Cloud). It accepts an IP only when at least two of them return the same one, so one wrong answer is not enough. A full check does this in 5 rounds on new connections (15 requests), so several IPs behind a load balancer all show up. The first check after install, Detect now and Verify again are full checks. The automatic checks after that ask each service once (3 requests).
help.result: Each IP the box sees is added or renewed for 30 days from that moment. An IP expires only when the box has not seen it for 30 days.
help.why: You cannot type an IP. Only an address the box really uses proves it belongs to your network, so nobody can verify someone else's address.
help.refuse: Private, reserved and shared carrier (CGNAT, 100.64.0.0/10) addresses are refused, because scanning them could hit other people.
help.limit: Detect now, Verify again and the DNS Check of a domain share 10 attempts per hour. Automatic checks do not use them: they can run as often as every minute, and a full check runs at most once an hour by itself. Every change is written to the audit log.

vulns.deepNote: Check a line before acting on it.
vulns.deepNoteInfo: Each line is what one template saw in the answer of this port: an exposed file, an admin page, a misconfiguration, or a technology it recognised (Info). A template that matched nothing is not listed and proves nothing.
vulns.noneTitleDeep: No exploited vulnerability matched the identified versions
vulns.noneBodyDeep: The deep scan found other things: see its findings below.

terms.title: Testing terms (deep scan)
terms.description: Accept once for this target: every scan of it is then a deep scan.
terms.descriptionInfo: Each tool is then used to its full capability. Without them, scans stay in the scope of the Scan now sentence: no OpenVAS, read-only checks only.
terms.none: Not accepted: scans of this target stay in the Scan now scope.
terms.changed: The testing terms changed since they were accepted, so scans are back in the Scan now scope until an administrator accepts them again.
terms.accepted: Accepted by {{by}}, {{time}}. Every scan of this target is a deep scan.
terms.who: Only an administrator with two-step sign-in can accept them; who and when go in the audit log. Withdrawing is always possible.
terms.needVerified: Verify ownership first; only then can the testing terms be accepted.
terms.cgnatLimit: If your router gets its address from your provider's shared range, ask your provider before accepting.
terms.cgnatLimitInfo: Vedette can tell carrier-grade NAT only when this box's own gateway is in 100.64.0.0/10; it cannot see your router's outside address.
terms.stops: Withdrawing them, or taking the disruptive checks out, stops a scan of this target that is running at the higher level.
terms.toastAccepted: Testing terms accepted. The next scan is a deep scan.
terms.toastWithdrawn: Testing terms withdrawn. The next scan is in the Scan now scope.

greenbone.title: Optional deep scan: OpenVAS
greenbone.description: Adds an OpenVAS scan to each deep scan of this box's public IP. Off by default.
greenbone.descriptionInfo: OpenVAS (Greenbone Community Edition, free, with the Greenbone Community Feed; not the paid Greenbone Enterprise) is an open-source vulnerability scanner that runs as its own containers next to Vedette. When it is on, each scan of the box's own verified public IP whose testing terms are accepted ends with an OpenVAS scan of that IP.

stateText.off: OpenVAS is off. Scans do not use it.
stateText.starting: OpenVAS is starting. The first start downloads its images (about 9 GB).
stateText.ready: OpenVAS is ready. The next scan of an IP of this box uses it.

greenbone.loading: OpenVAS is loading its feed (first time takes about 2 hours)
greenbone.what: It looks at your public IP from outside without logging in, with the OpenVAS "Full and fast" tests, only once that IP's testing terms are accepted (Ownership tab): every non-disruptive check, active ones included, with safe checks on; with the disruptive checks ticked, brute force, default accounts, denial of service and generic web application scanning too, with safe checks off (this can run up to the time cap).
greenbone.apart: Its results are shown in their own section of each scan. They never replace or hide what Vedette found by version, and finding nothing is not proof that nothing is affected.
greenbone.weekly: While it is on, Vedette updates the OpenVAS feed once a week, never during a scan, and only with 60 GB free.
greenbone.offKeeps: Turning it off stops its containers and keeps its images and data, so turning it on again does not download them again.
greenbone.feedTestsInfo: The date of the Greenbone Community Feed that OpenVAS reports it has loaded (version {{version}}). The feed comes with the first load when OpenVAS is turned on; after that Vedette updates it once a week.
greenbone.feedFirstDone: First full feed load done; the weekly update has not run yet
greenbone.feedFirstDoneAt: First full feed load done (OpenVAS turned on {{time}}); the weekly update has not run yet
greenbone.needs: Needs about 50 GB of disk and about 2 hours to load the OpenVAS feed the first time.
greenbone.needsInfo: The box must have at least 6 GB of memory (under 8 GB, also 2 GB of swap) and 60 GB free.
greenbone.swapNote: The first feed load uses swap on a box under 8 GB.
greenbone.swapNoteInfo: On a 7 GB box it used about 2 GB of swap.
greenbone.offWaiting: Stopping the OpenVAS containers… this can take a few minutes.
greenbone.heldOn: It is still turned on from before: turn it off to stop its containers. Its data is kept.
greenbone.toastOn: OpenVAS is starting. Loading its feed takes about 2 hours the first time.
greenbone.toastOff: OpenVAS is off. Its data is kept.

results.title: OpenVAS results (unauthenticated, QoD ≥ 70)
results.header: OpenVAS looked at this IP from outside without logging in.
results.headerInfo: Finding nothing is not proof the services are not affected (distributions backport fixes). For the same reason, on Ubuntu or Debian a result read from a version banner can be a false positive, so Vedette's own package-based result wins when both exist.
results.caption: What OpenVAS reported on this IP
results.noneTitle: OpenVAS reported no high or medium result with QoD 70 or more
results.noneBody: Not proof that the services are not affected: the exploited CVEs above still stand.
results.noneBodyInfo: That is one outside look without logging in, not proof that the services are not affected. The exploited CVEs above still stand.
results.notRunTitle: OpenVAS did not scan this time
results.notRunBody: OpenVAS is not set up for this scan.
results.runningBody: OpenVAS started at {{time}} and runs for up to 90 minutes. The results of the other checks are already saved; its results are added here when it finishes.
results.runningBodyNoTime: OpenVAS runs for up to 90 minutes. The results of the other checks are already saved; its results are added here when it finishes.
results.partialLine: OpenVAS was stopped after 90 minutes; these are the results it had found by then.
results.partialNoneBody: A partial outside look, not proof that the services are not affected.
results.partialNoneBodyInfo: By then it had found no high or medium result with QoD 70 or more. That is a partial outside look, not proof that the services are not affected.
results.failedTitle: OpenVAS did not finish this scan
results.failedBody: OpenVAS failed, so its results are not shown. The box log has the error.
results.stoppedTitle: OpenVAS was stopped before it finished
results.stoppedBody: OpenVAS was stopped before it finished, so its results are not shown. The results of the other checks above are kept.
results.domainLine: OpenVAS did not finish every address of this domain; these are the results it found. The "Not checked" list below says which address ended early and why.
results.endedTitle: OpenVAS ended the scan before it finished
results.endedBody: OpenVAS ended the scan before it finished. The "Not checked" list below says why.
results.endedLine: OpenVAS ended the scan before it finished; these are the results it had found by then. The "Not checked" list below says why.
results.startedEnded: OpenVAS started at {{time}} and ended at {{end}}.
results.again: OpenVAS ran again on its own for this scan, on the open ports it found.
results.stoppedNotShown: Its results are not shown. The results of the other checks above are kept.

stop.shutdown: Stopped at {{time}}: Vedette shut down while OpenVAS ran (an update, a restart or a stop of the service).
stop.restart: Stopped: Vedette restarted while OpenVAS ran. It noticed when it started again at {{time}}.
stop.restartNoTime: Stopped: Vedette restarted while OpenVAS ran.
stop.unknown: Stopped at {{time}}: someone pressed Stop or Vedette shut down (an update or a restart). This scan is older than the version of Vedette that records which of the two.
stop.unknownNoTime: Stopped before it finished; the time was not recorded for this older scan. The reason is one of: someone pressed Stop, Vedette shut down (an update or a restart), the External exposure module was switched off, or the testing terms were withdrawn or lowered.
stop.module_off: Stopped at {{time}}: the External exposure module was switched off.
stop.terms: Stopped at {{time}}: {{by}} withdrew or lowered the testing terms of this target.

results.notesHeader: Hardening suggestions, such as weak SSH settings or TCP timestamps.
results.notesHeaderInfo: The Low results of OpenVAS are not alerts and are not counted anywhere.
results.notesCaption: OpenVAS hardening notes on this IP

again.note: Checks the open TCP ports this scan found ({{ports}}) for up to 90 minutes. Its result replaces this OpenVAS part; the other results above stay as they are.
again.busy: Another scan is running on this box. Wait for it to finish.
again.terms: OpenVAS runs only under the testing terms, and they are not accepted for this target.
again.notReady: OpenVAS cannot scan now: it is starting, loading its feed or not available.
again.notReadyLink: See its state: External exposure, Optional deep scan
again.wait: Wait until {{time}}: at most one scan of a target every 10 minutes, and OpenVAS again counts as one.

greenbone.offReason: OpenVAS is off on this box.
greenbone.offLink: Turn it on: External exposure, Optional deep scan

web.title: Web findings (passive)
web.description: Hints ZAP noticed while reading the pages, not exploited vulnerabilities.
web.descriptionInfo: ZAP looked at the pages without sending forms; these are things it noticed. They are hints from reading the pages and the server's answers, not known exploited vulnerabilities. When ZAP reads a version that has an exploited CVE (a JavaScript library, a Server or X-Powered-By header), that CVE is listed with the exploited CVEs.
web.caption: What ZAP noticed on the web pages

fix.title: Fix this
fix.description: Things to change: a vulnerable JavaScript library, a server that gives away its version, an error page that shows internals, a password sent without encryption.
fix.caption: Web findings to fix

hardening.title: Hardening
hardening.description: Settings that make the site harder to attack: missing security headers, cookie flags, cross-site settings. Each row keeps ZAP's own risk.
hardening.caption: Web hardening suggestions

web.noneTitle: ZAP noticed nothing on the pages it looked at
web.noneBody: That does not prove the pages are safe.
web.noneBodyInfo: ZAP only reads what the server sends, and sends no forms.
web.notScannedBody: The passive web scan did not look at any page in this scan.
web.cweLink: CWE-{{id}} (opens the MITRE page in a new tab)

checked.title: What was checked
checked.description: What this scan sent and compared, and what it did not check.
checked.descriptionInfo: A scan that did not check something says nothing about it.
checked.older: This scan was made before Vedette listed what each scan checks.

outside.title: What the Internet sees
outside.description: What Shodan has seen on {{ip}} from outside, beside our own scan.
outside.descriptionInfo: Our scan runs from inside your network, so it reaches {{ip}} through your router. Shodan scans the whole Internet from outside and keeps what it finds, so it can show ports your router opens to the Internet but hides from this box.
outside.never: Vedette has not asked Shodan about {{ip}}.
outside.neverInfo: Nothing is sent until an administrator chooses Check what Shodan has seen.
outside.notEligible: Only a verified public IP that the box goes out through now can be checked with Shodan.
outside.confirmBody: Your public IP {{ip}} is sent to Shodan (internetdb.shodan.io). Shodan learns that someone asked about it. Nothing else is sent to Shodan.
outside.confirmBodyInfo: First the box may re-check that it still goes out through {{ip}} (the same check as before a scan).
outside.waiting: Checking that the box still uses this IP, then asking Shodan… this can take up to a minute.
outside.askedInfo: Shodan updates this data about once a week and does not say when it last saw this IP.
outside.noRecord: Shodan has no record of {{ip}}: it has not seen an open port there.
outside.notScanned: Our scan has not run on {{ip}} yet, so there is nothing to compare with.
outside.portsTitle: Open ports, Shodan and our scan

port.both: Shodan and our scan both saw {{port}} open.
port.shodanOnly: Shodan saw {{port}} open; our scan did not.
port.oursOnly: Our scan saw {{port}} open; Shodan did not.

hint.shodanOnly: Is it meant to be open? If not, close it on the router or firewall.
hint.shodanOnlyInfo: A port only the Internet sees is usually one your router opens on its outside interface, or forwards only for outside traffic.
hint.oursOnly: Shodan may not have scanned {{port}} since it opened (its data is about a week old), or the port answers only from inside.

outside.hostnames: Names Shodan links to this IP: {{list}}.
outside.vulnsNote: Shodan guesses these from the software versions it saw. They are Shodan's claim: Vedette has not confirmed them, and the Exploited vulnerabilities above are Vedette's own check.
outside.vuln: Shodan lists {{cve}}; Vedette has not confirmed it.

deep.title: Deep scan by address
deep.description: The deep scan of each public IPv4 address this domain's names resolve to.
deep.descriptionInfo: With this domain's testing terms accepted, each public IPv4 address its names resolve to gets the deep scan, whatever serves it: every TCP port, service versions, exploited vulnerabilities, templates and OpenVAS when it is on; its names keep the passive web scan by name. At most 3 addresses a run, the least recently tried first; the others follow in the next runs.
deep.caption: Addresses of this domain's names and their deep scan
deep.found: {{services}} services, {{vulns}} exploited CVEs, {{web}} web alerts, {{openvas}} OpenVAS results

why.waiting: Not scanned this run: the cap of 3 addresses was reached.
why.fence: Checked by name only: this box needs the Vedette host's domain fence (update the box).
why.refused: The check right before the scan refused it (the name moved, or the terms changed), so nothing was sent.
why.incomplete: Service identification did not finish, so its ports are not known this run; it goes back in line.

moved.title: Open exposures and What the Internet sees are now on each target.
moved.info: Select a target in the list to read its results, its open exposures and, for a public IP, what the Internet sees. The number in the last column is that target's open exposures.

openNever: This target has not been scanned yet, so no open port is known.

settings.scanDescription: Scan speed and the addresses a scan never touches are shared by every scan of the box.
settings.scanReason: They are set once for the whole box.

schedule.label: Scheduled scan
schedule.offLong: Scheduled scans are off: this target is scanned only when someone presses the scan button.
schedule.info: The box scans this target by itself, counted from the start of its newest scan, only inside the scan window under Settings, Scanning, Safety and only while its ownership proof holds and its testing terms are accepted. It is the same scan as the scan button, except that a scheduled scan never includes the disruptive checks, even when they are accepted: those run only when a person presses the scan button. OpenVAS joins only when it is turned on under Settings. Anything new it finds (an open port, an admin page, a certificate expiring within 30 days, an exploited vulnerability) is sent to your alert channels; no change, no message.
